newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on commission sales, hedges.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on commission sales, hedges.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended down on commission, local selling and farmer hedges, traders said.

"Commission houses and locals sold, the rise in soybeans didn't give us a push, there were moderate hedges," a trader said. About 200 Mar-July spread at $2, May-July at even money, Mar-May $1.50 and Jan-Mar $1. January futures crush profit margin rose to -39.86 from midday at -42.31 based on January soyoil and meal. Volume was moderate.
January canola lost $1.50 to $410.20 a tonne, March fell $2.20 to $411.50. January flax lost $0.30 to $366.60 while March was unchanged at $368.50 as Cargill sold, traders said.
Commission houses sold 75 December feed peas up US$2 to US$203, UGG sold May down US$0.50 to US$198.50, traders said.
February western barley lost $4.40 to $140.80 on local profit taking, traders said. Cargill sold 200 Feb-May spread at $0.70 another 500 spread at $1, Feb-Mar was at even money.
"Locals are taking profits ahead of the weekend after we had a sustained five day rally in the barley," a trader said.
UGG sold December feed wheat down $4.70 to $171.50 while March fell $4.30 to $172.50 on commission selling, traders said. UGG bought the Dec-Mar spread at even money, traders said. No oats traded.
(All values in Canadian dollars per tonne except peas, oats).
